note_revisions.title: 48 laws of power
note_revisions.body:
The 48 Laws of Power

Law 1: Never Outshine the Master
Make your bosses feel smarter and more powerful than they are to keep your position secure.

Law 2: Never Put Too Much Trust in Friends, Learn How to Use Enemies
Friends can betray you out of envy or familiarity. Former enemies may work harder because they have more to prove.

Law 3: Conceal Your Intentions
Keep people uncertain about your plans. If they cannot see your real objective, they cannot easily interfere with it.

Law 4: Always Say Less Than Necessary
The more you talk, the more information you reveal. Speak carefully and let your words carry weight.

Law 5: So Much Depends on Reputation—Guard It With Your Life
Your reputation can determine how people treat you before they even know you. Protect it and respond quickly when it is threatened.

Law 6: Court Attention at All Costs
Being invisible makes it difficult to gain influence. Find ways to make yourself noticed and remembered.

Law 7: Get Others to Do the Work for You, but Always Take the Credit
Use the skills, knowledge, and resources of others to achieve your goals efficiently. Make sure your contribution and leadership are recognized.

Law 8: Make Other People Come to You
Create enough value or desire that people seek you out rather than constantly chasing them.

Law 9: Win Through Your Actions, Never Through Argument
Arguments often create resistance. Demonstrating that you are right is usually more powerful than trying to convince someone with words.

Law 10: Infection: Avoid the Unhappy and Unlucky
People's attitudes and problems can influence those around them. Be careful about allowing consistently negative or destructive people into your inner circle.

Law 11: Learn to Keep People Dependent on You
Become valuable by developing skills, knowledge, resources, or connections that others cannot easily replace.

**Law 12: Use Selective Honesty and Generosity to Disarm Your Victim**
A well-timed act of honesty or generosity can lower people's defenses and make them more receptive to you.

**Law 13: When Asking for Help, Appeal to People's Self-Interest**
People are more motivated when they understand what they will gain. Show them how helping you benefits them too.

**Law 14: Pose as a Friend, Work as a Spy**
Pay attention to what people reveal about themselves. Understanding their motives, priorities, and weaknesses gives you an advantage.

**Law 15: Crush Your Enemy Totally**
If someone is determined to destroy your position, leaving them with the ability to retaliate can create future problems. Resolve serious conflicts decisively.

**Law 16: Use Absence to Increase Respect and Honor**
Constant availability can make you seem less valuable. Strategic distance can increase appreciation and respect.

**Law 17: Keep Others in Suspended Terror: Cultivate an Air of Unpredictability**
If people cannot completely predict your next move, they will be more cautious about challenging or manipulating you.

**Law 18: Do Not Build Fortresses to Protect Yourself—Isolation Is Dangerous**
Protecting yourself by completely withdrawing from others can cut you off from valuable information and opportunities. Maintain useful relationships.

**Law 19: Know Who You're Dealing With—Do Not Offend the Wrong Person**
Different people react differently to pressure, criticism, and humiliation. Understand someone's character before deciding how to deal with them.

**Law 20: Do Not Commit to Anyone**
Avoid becoming unnecessarily tied to one side of a conflict. Maintaining independence gives you flexibility and bargaining power.

**Law 21: Play a Sucker to Catch a Sucker—Seem Dumber Than Your Mark**
People often become careless when they believe they are smarter than you. Do not always feel the need to demonstrate your intelligence.

**Law 22: Use the Surrender Tactic: Transform Weakness Into Power**
When you are in a position of weakness, fighting blindly can make things worse. Sometimes stepping back gives you time to recover and regain control.

**Law 23: Concentrate Your Forces**
Do not spread your time, money, energy, and attention across too many objectives. Focus your resources where they can produce the greatest result.

**Law 24: Play the Perfect Courtier**
Learn how to navigate social environments with tact, diplomacy, confidence, and awareness of other people's egos.

**Law 25: Re-Create Yourself**
Do not allow other people to permanently define who you are. Deliberately shape your identity, image, and direction.

**Law 26: Keep Your Hands Clean**
Avoid being directly associated with unnecessary scandals, failures, and conflicts. Protect your reputation by managing how your actions are perceived.

**Law 27: Play on People's Need to Believe to Create a Cultlike Following**
People naturally seek meaning, belonging, and something to believe in. Give them a compelling vision, while being careful not to exploit or manipulate them.

**Law 28: Enter Action With Boldness**
Hesitation communicates weakness and creates opportunities for others to interfere. Once you have decided, act with confidence.

**Law 29: Plan All the Way to the End**
Think beyond your immediate objective. Consider the consequences, obstacles, opportunities, and final outcome before taking major action.

**Law 30: Make Your Accomplishments Seem Effortless**
People are impressed by results that appear natural and controlled. Develop your skills so thoroughly that excellence looks effortless.

**Law 31: Control the Options: Get Others to Play With the Cards You Deal**
Instead of forcing people into one choice, give them options that all work in your favor.

Law 32: Play to People's Fantasies
People are often attracted to hope, dreams, and possibilities more than harsh reality. Understand what people want to believe and connect your message to it.

**Law 33: Discover Each Person's Thumbscrew**
Everyone has motivations, fears, desires, insecurities, or ambitions that influence their decisions. Understanding these factors helps you communicate effectively.

**Law 34: Be Royal in Your Own Fashion: Act Like a King to Be Treated Like One**
The way you carry yourself influences how others perceive and treat you. Demonstrate confidence, self-respect, and standards.

**Law 35: Master the Art of Timing**
Knowing what to do is not enough. Learn when to act, when to wait, and when an opportunity has reached its proper moment.

**Law 36: Disdain Things You Cannot Have: Ignoring Them Is the Best Revenge**
Obsessing over what you cannot obtain gives it power over you. Sometimes the strongest response is to stop giving it attention.

**Law 37: Create Compelling Spectacles**
People remember what they see and experience more easily than abstract explanations. Use strong presentation and memorable moments to communicate your ideas.

**Law 38: Think as You Like but Behave Like Others**
You do not need to reveal every unconventional belief you have. Understand the culture around you and know when to adapt your outward behavior.

**Law 39: Stir Up Waters to Catch Fish**
Emotional people are easier to influence than calm people. Maintain your composure while recognizing when others are losing theirs.

**Law 40: Despise the Free Lunch**
Nothing is truly free when it creates obligations, dependency, or hidden costs. Value independence and understand the price behind attractive offers.

**Law 41: Avoid Stepping Into a Great Man's Shoes**
Following a highly successful predecessor can create unrealistic comparisons. Establish your own identity rather than living in someone else's shadow.

**Law 42: Strike the Shepherd and the Sheep Will Scatter**
Some groups are held together primarily by one influential person. Addressing the central source of disruption can sometimes resolve a larger conflict.

**Law 43: Work on the Hearts and Minds of Others**
People cooperate more willingly when they feel understood and respected. Influence people by understanding their emotions and motivations.

**Law 44: Disarm and Infuriate With the Mirror Effect**
Reflecting someone's behavior or attitudes back to them can expose their own actions and make them reconsider how they behave.

**Law 45: Preach the Need for Change, but Never Reform Too Much at Once**
People may welcome improvement but resist having everything changed immediately. Introduce major changes gradually enough for people to adapt.

**Law 46: Never Appear Too Perfect**
Perfection can create envy and resentment. Allowing people to see that you are human can make you more relatable and less threatening.

**Law 47: Do Not Go Past the Mark You Aimed For; In Victory, Learn When to Stop**
Success can create overconfidence. Once you have achieved your objective, know when to stop before greed or ambition turns a victory into a loss.

**Law 48: Assume Formlessness**
Do not become rigid or predictable. Stay adaptable and change your strategy when circumstances change.

notes.title: 47 laws of power
notes.body:
The First 10 Laws of Power

Law 1: Never Outshine the Master
Make your bosses feel smarter and more powerful than they are to keep your position secure.

Law 2: Never Put Too Much Trust in Friends, Learn How to Use Enemies
Friends can betray you quickly out of envy. A hired enemy has more to prove and will work harder.

Law 3: Conceal Your Intentions
Keep people off-balance and in the dark. If they have no clue what you are up to, they cannot prepare a defense.

Law 4: Always Say Less Than Necessary
The more you talk, the more common you look and the higher the risk that you will say something foolish.

Law 5: So Much Depends on Reputation – Guard It with Your Life
A strong reputation helps you win before a fight even starts. Destroy your rivals by poking holes in theirs.

Law 6: Court Attention at All Cost
Everything is judged by appearances. Stand out, be colorful, and never get lost in the crowd.

Law 7: Get Others to do the Work for You, but Always Take the Credit
Use the skills and effort of other people to save your own time. It makes you look incredibly efficient.

Law 8: Make Other People Come to You – Use Bait if Necessary
When you force the other person to act, you stay in control. Make them abandon their own plans to meet yours.

Law 9: Win Through Your Actions, Never Through Argument
A victory won through words is brief and breeds resentment. It is much more powerful to get agreement through what you do.

Law 10: Infection: Avoid the Unhappy and Unlucky
You can die from someone else’s misery. Emotional states are as infectious as diseases, so associate only with the happy and fortunate.

Law 45: Preach the Need for Change, but Never Reform Too Much at Once
People may welcome improvement but resist having everything changed immediately. Introduce major changes gradually enough for people to adapt.

Law 46: Never Appear Too Perfect
Perfection can create envy and resentment. Allowing people to see that you are human can make you more relatable and less threatening.

Law 47: Do Not Go Past the Mark You Aimed For; In Victory, Learn When to Stop
Success can create overconfidence. Once you have achieved your objective, know when to stop before greed or ambition turns a victory into a loss.

Law 48: Assume Formlessness
Do not become rigid or predictable. Stay adaptable and change your strategy when circumstances change.
